findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 changes username-link lightness from 30% to 70% in light themes, reducing contrast; preserve 30% for `$primary` and 70% for `$secondary`.
app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 changes `h3` lightness from 20% to 50% in light themes, fading headings and making their color identical to `h4`; use the intended 20%/80% pairing.

app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 and app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:497 change `.name` lightness from 30% to 50% in light themes, reducing contrast and removing the color distinction from `.title`; preserve the 30%/70% pairing.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 uses a reversed 30%/70% pairing for `.custom-message-length` instead of 70%/30%, changing its light-theme appearance and making it inconsistent with the equivalent desktop rule.

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 changes `h3` lightness from 20% to 50% in light themes, fading headings and making their color identical to `h4`; use the intended 20%/80% pairing.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for mobile/topic-post.scss line 179-182, the original code was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and it was changed to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The finding correctly identifies that the lightness value changed from 20% to 50% for light themes. This is inconsistent with other similar changes in the codebase where 20% lightness is paired with 80% (e.g., desktop/topic-post.scss line 318, 379, etc. show `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`). The h4 element at line 187 uses 50%/50%, so this change makes h3 identical to h4 in color, which appears to be an unintended inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 uses a reversed 30%/70% pairing for `.custom-message-length` instead of 70%/30%, changing its light-theme appearance and making it inconsistent with the equivalent desktop rule.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff for mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This uses 30%/70% instead of the expected 70%/30% pattern used consistently throughout the rest of the diff. The desktop equivalent in desktop/modal.scss line 94 uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` which is the correct 70%/30% pattern. This reversal would change the light-theme appearance (making it darker instead of maintaining the same lightness) and creates an inconsistency between mobile and desktop.
